title: Stochastic phase-sampling allocator for balanced latency/throughput
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem:
Current deterministic phase-splitting policies create brittle boundaries that can oscillate under multi-tenant load: small bursts get favorably scheduled while medium-length requests are either starved or forced into larger decode batches that blow tail latency. Existing fairness schemes rely on strict quotas or proportional slicing which can be gamed by adversarial request shapes and can create periodic throughput cliffs.

Proposal (high level):
Introduce a Stochastic Phase-Sampling Allocator (SPSA) that: 
- Uses probabilistic micro-phase sampling to decide prefill->decode split points instead of fixed heuristics. The sampler draws split candidates from a distribution conditioned on request length, kernel cost estimate, and recent service latency for that tenant/route.
- Maintains per-tenant fairness credits that accrue continuously (fractional tokens) and are consumed probabilistically when a tenant's request is selected. This decouples fairness from hard slicing and reduces deterministic starvation patterns.
- Exposes a single tunable "temperature" parameter per-tenant/route to bias the sampler toward low-latency (cold low-temperature -> prefer early splits) or high-throughput (high-temperature -> accept larger decode phases). The platform can auto-tune temperature using recent p95 vs throughput tradeoff curves.
- Integrates kernel-selection signals: the sampler prefers split points that align with efficient kernel boundaries (e.g., prefers splits that enable fused-kernel decode paths or avoid large attention windows) to reduce token compute overhead introduced by micro-phases.

Why this is different/beneficial:
- Reduces oscillatory scheduling behaviour by introducing controlled randomness, which empirically smooths allocation under multi-tenant bursts.
- Provides a continuous knob (temperature) for latency/throughput tradeoffs per tenant without requiring structural config changes or separate QoS buckets.
- Keeps fairness guarantees in expectation rather than via brittle periodic quotas, reducing long-tail starvation events.
- Makes scheduler decisions kernel-aware, improving unit compute efficiency for micro-phase patterns.

Acceptance criteria (minimal):
1) Simulation harness: SPSA simulation with synthetic job mixes (short-chatty, long-generative, bursty-burst) produces >=5% reduction in p95 latency for latency-oriented temperature, with <7% throughput regression for throughput-oriented settings (compared to current baseline policy).
2) Fairness metric (Jain index over per-tenant served tokens) stays within 5% of baseline during steady-state and improves under bursty adversarial patterns.
3) End-to-end integration: scheduler emits telemetry for chosen split points, sampled temperature, and kernel preference tags. Telemetry schema and dashboards added to console-telemetry.
4) Experimental rollout plan defined: canary on 10% of traffic with auto-rollback when p95 increases >10% or error rate increases >0.5%.

Implementation plan (phases):
- Phase 0 (design & sim): finalize sampler distribution (mixture of truncated-normal + power-law tail), fairness credit accrual formula, and kernel alignment heuristics. Simulate against historical traces. (Owner: Marcus Li)
- Phase 1 (prototype): implement lightweight in-memory sampler module in scheduler path behind feature flag; add telemetry events and an offline evaluator. (Owner: Marcus Li)
- Phase 2 (bench): run microbench and integration perf tests on dedicated pool, measure kernel-utilization delta and impact on batching efficiency. (Owner: Perf infra)
- Phase 3 (canary): roll out to 10% traffic, monitor SLOs and fairness index, iterate on temperature auto-tuner. (Owner: Oncall/Release Eng)

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: Randomized decisions can increase overall compute cost if micro-phases cause more kernel transitions. Mitigation: kernel-aware preference and a conservative default temperature under which sampler collapses to baseline deterministic split.
- Risk: Complexity in telemetry and reasoning about per-tenant temperature. Mitigation: dashboard + automated suggestions that map temperature to expected p50/p95/throughput impact.
- Risk: Long warm-up for temperature auto-tuner. Mitigation: initialize temperature from historical route profile and use conservative learning rate.

Metrics to collect:
- p50/p90/p95/request latency for prefill and decode stages
- tokens/sec throughput and tokens-per-GPU-second cost estimate
- kernel transition count per request (micro-phase sensitivity)
- fairness index (Jain) across tenants and starvation rate (#requests waiting > threshold)
- temperature distribution histogram and correlation with latency/throughput

Rollout/experiment design:
- A/B test against baseline on production traces replay in cluster-sim then canary 10% traffic for 48h.
- Run adversarial trace (many short bursts + some long requests) to validate fairness credits keep starvation low.
- Iterate on temperature default and auto-tuner window size.

Documentation & artifacts:
- Design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/RUNTIME/SPSA (placeholder)
- Simulation notebooks: drive.google.com/open?id=1-sim-spsa (placeholder)
